title: A peer's board write that is still landing refuses an unrelated commit: WriteSet renames board.json before wip.md, and doctor counts the old view beside the new canon as a hand edit
body:
Found by dc on 2026-10-22, measured on 2026-10-23 on vc's order (ORDER dc-1 unit 3), from the TO MEASURE AND FILE line in intent/wip.md.

## What happened

dc's fold commit on 2026-10-22 was refused by the commit gate's doctor with a counted view-skew on cc's `wip.md`, 3266 bytes on disk and 1410 rendered. cc's fold was writing at that moment. The same commit passed when re-issued.

## Mechanism, read and then driven

`WriteSet::commit` (`intentsvcs/src/write_set.rs`) lands a write's files one at a time, a temp file and a rename each, in path order. For a board that order is `board.json`, then the inbox views, then `wip.md`. Doctor's skew check (`views::skew`) renders each view from the canon on disk. So between the first rename and the last, a reader sees a NEW `board.json` beside an OLD `wip.md`: the view disagrees with its own canon, and the counted `view-skew` arm reads it as a hand edit ("either it was edited by hand, or the store changed after it was rendered"). In a peer's write that is still landing, the gate's doctor counts it, and an unrelated commit is refused.

The state just before the views land is not the problem. With a board write whose views cannot land (aa's directory read-only), doctor raises only an uncounted `store-stale` advisory, and an unrelated commit passes (`refs/bank/dc/skew/repro.sh`, blob 52fdfd900e26).

`refs/bank/dc/skew/repro2.sh` (blob 65ef1da7cd7d) runs on the installed 3.2.5 pair (2e0e9215d), in a scratch project with the gate installed and two nodes:

- HELD STILL. After a normal board write by aa, aa's previous `wip.md` is put back beside the new `board.json`. This is the disk between the renames. Doctor exits 1 with `view-skew -- 1 finding: intent/whiteboard/aa/wip.md -- generated view differs from the model (845 bytes on disk, 772 rendered, first difference at byte 185)`. bb's unrelated commit through the gate is refused on that finding. Once aa's view lands (`intent wb touch --node aa`), the same commit passes.
- LIVE. aa makes 80 board writes in a loop while bb's doctor reads in a loop: 5 of 19 reads counted a view-skew.

So a node's commit is refused whenever its gate's doctor reads during a peer's board write. A fold is a burst of such writes, which is when nodes commit most.

## Expected

A view that is a write in progress is not a hand edit, and a peer's write in progress refuses no one's commit. Two shapes:

- **(a) Provenance, in doctor.** The file index records the bytes of every view the store writes, and `record_landed` updates it only after the whole set has landed. So during the window the old `wip.md` on disk still matches the index's record for it. A view whose bytes equal the index's record is the store's own last render, not an edit. It can be reported uncounted, as the views lagging their canon with `intent wb touch` or `sync --to-disk` as the remedy, while a view that matches neither the render nor the record stays a counted hand edit.
- **(b) Scope, in the gate.** The commit gate counts a view-skew only on paths the commit stages, and shows the rest uncounted.

(a) keeps doctor's answer true for every caller, and (b) narrows only the gate. A doctor that waits on the writer's lock is a third shape, and it puts a wait on every gate.

## Spec (vc, 2026-10-23, under hv's go)

LANE: unassigned today; the spec is here for the next lane, cc's area (the store's writes and doctor). SHAPE: option (a), provenance from the file index. Doctor judges a view against the record the file index holds for it, which record_landed updates only after the whole write set lands, so a peer's old `wip.md` beside its new `board.json` still matches its record mid-window and is reported as store-stale, uncounted, never as a hand edit; a view that matches neither its index record nor the store's render stays a counted hand edit. Option (b), scoping the commit gate's doctor, is refused: the gate is the right door and the judge is what is wrong, so the judge is fixed. PROOF: dc's reproductions (refs/bank/dc/skew/repro.sh and repro2.sh) held still at the mid-window state: doctor exits 0 and a peer's commit passes, red on the base; doctor's hand-edit arms stay green. Rust, worktree, bank, the whole intentsvcs and intent-cli suites. CLOSES WHEN: the bank lands and `intent issues close 0630` names the sha.

## Resolution

Fixed by 491c1cc33 for 3.2.6. Doctor judges a view against the file index's record for it, as the spec chose, and a view that matches its last render while its write lands is reported store-stale, uncounted, with `intent wb touch` or `sync --to-disk` as the remedy; a view that matches neither the render nor the record stays a counted hand edit. THE SPEC'S PREMISE, CORRECTED FORWARD: the file index was not a provenance record. A scan recorded what it met, and a second scan of the same bytes marked them clean, so the first build of this fix ((B), excusing a view whose bytes equal its row) was proved unsound by its own arm: two `doctor` runs in a freshly initialised project took a hand edit of `todo.md` to clean. On vc's rulings of 2026-10-23, a view's row is now the record of what its renderer wrote or a projection found already right, and a scan never writes over a renderer's `Clean` row ((S), 18:38Z). A view the scan meets with no row takes the scan's entry as `Changed`, which `doctor` never reads as a render, and under the daemon's ingest a view whose row is not `Clean` takes it again ((A) and (B), 20:18Z). Those two close what (S) alone cost, both measured before anything landed. A file at a view's path that no projection writes was re-ingested at every thirty-second backstop. A cover no renderer had recorded, a fresh clone's, read as new at every sync, so a hand edit of its Objective was neither carried nor refused. PROOF: the mid-window state is the arm `a_view_a_write_is_still_landing_is_store_stale_and_refuses_no_commit`, beside four arms on hand edits and recorded renders in the same file, three daemon arms in `daemon_watch.rs`, and `info_round_trip_reaches_the_store`. All of them were judged on one composition with the templates and 0633: the cargo half green at 2e36149a89ce and the shell half at 9b11789c0486. The issue's title names `WriteSet`'s rename order, which is unchanged: the judge was fixed, not the writer.
